description: Same-runner A/B for the gRPC RPC-deadline response path (issue #6904). One hosted runner builds the reference and candidate revisions with the same toolchain and ci-release profile, then measures both in alternating rounds against one proto_backend and one proto_bench. Eight cells cross the RPC shape (unary, server-streaming), authentication (none, key_auth), and the client deadline (none, grpc-timeout). The deadline-free cells exercise no RPC-deadline code in either revision and are the null control; the primary estimate is the difference-in-differences of the candidate/reference ratio between a deadline cell and its deadline-free sibling, which cancels runner drift and every revision change outside the deadline path. Every deadline cell must prove the backend received grpc-timeout on every call, each gateway lifetime runs a stalled-stream probe that only the gateway's deadline can end, and each key_auth lifetime proves a keyless call is refused. The gateway runs the benchmark regime of run_protocol_test.sh (FERRUM_MAX_RESPONSE_BODY_SIZE_BYTES=0 and FERRUM_RESPONSE_BUFFER_CUTOFF_BYTES=0, which select the direct streaming gRPC response branch rather than the default size-limited coalescing branch) with FERRUM_WORKER_THREADS=2, so the per-frame cost does not transfer one-to-one to a default-configured gateway. Throughput and CPU per call are primary endpoints; p99 is secondary and can only mark a regression.
